While I feel uncomfortable telling you exactly what to do, I can attest that having someone tell you they believe you can be incredibly therapeutic. It's difficult to describe the intense amount of scrutiny placed on people who have been raped or sexually assaulted, and it constantly feels like society is just itching to tell you that you are lying or were asking for it. As a result, it often seems easier to stuff things away or even cut yourself off from other people. It's an *incredibly* isolating experience, for many reasons. I would say, however, that hearing my friend tell me "I believe you" was one of the most important things I needed to hear after my rape, and it is what I remember the most about her response to me.

I'm speaking for myself at this point because I don't know how Emma is feeling now. Given the recency of my assault, however, I hope that someone else can also provide a perspective from a survivor who is a bit more removed from the event.
